page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% at 2921.98. However, multi-core scaling is limited, as evidenced by a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 2926.09 and a poor Geekbench multi-core score of 2013.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable constraint, with small-block cached read speeds at 136.6 GB/sec and large-block uncached write speeds at 23.42 GB/sec, both falling into the lower percentiles. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, perform at average levels, while database operations and software compilation benchmarks show weaker relative throughput.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile and low resource footprint, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory allocations or local storage. The lack of bundled storage and low memory-to-vCPU ratio represent clear tradeoffs. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded processing, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale LLM inference tasks where single-core performance is prioritized over memory capacity.
